items.t: Worn valve stem seals make the V8 burn oil
items.job: Replace valve stem seals (both cylinder banks)
items.note: Labor-heavy job; some shops can do it without removing the cylinder heads.

items.t: Plastic cooling parts crack and the engine overheats
items.job: Replace water pump and thermostat

items.t: Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak oil
items.job: Replace valve cover gaskets

items.t: Automatic transmission shifts harshly or leaks fluid
items.job: Replace mechatronic sleeve, filter pan and fluid

items.t: Rod bearing wear on the M6 V10
items.job: Replace connecting rod bearings and rod bolts (preventive or at first sign of wear)
items.note: Parts from the Turner Motorsport E60 M5/E63 M6 rod bearing kit ($1,041-$1,286). BMWTuning says to expect at least $2,000 in shop labor plus $800 or more in parts; the hours here reflect that labor figure. If a bearing has already spun, an engine rebuild or replacement costs far more.

items.t: Throttle actuators fail on the M6
items.job: Rebuild or replace failed throttle actuator(s) and recalibrate
items.note: Low end is one actuator sent out for a metal-gear rebuild ($390, Beisan Systems); high end is two new genuine BMW actuators (about $760 each at BimmerWorld). BMWTuning puts shop labor at about $250-$400 (2-3 hours) and advises replacing both at once.

items.t: iDrive screen freezes, reboots or goes blank
items.job: Diagnose and update or replace iDrive head unit
items.note: Low end is a software update only.

items.t: Convertible top stops or works slowly
items.job: Repair convertible top hydraulic pump or cylinder
items.note: A failed microswitch costs far less.

items.t: Battery drains overnight
items.job: Diagnose parasitic drain and replace battery

items.t: Front control arm bushings wear and the wheel shakes when braking
items.job: Replace front control arms (pair) and align

items.t: Engine computer can stall the engine (recall)
items.job: Recall repair at a BMW dealer
items.note: Free at a BMW dealer. Check your VIN to see if it was already done.

items.t: Static discharge can stall the V8 in cold weather (recall)
items.job: Recall repair at a BMW dealer
items.note: Free at a BMW dealer. Check your VIN to see if it was already done.

items.t: Brake vacuum pump valve can leak oil and weaken the brakes (recall)
items.job: Recall repair at a BMW dealer
items.note: Free at a BMW dealer. Check your VIN to see if it was already done.

items.t: Twin-turbo V8 burns oil from worn valve stem seals
items.job: Replace valve stem seals (twin-turbo V8)
items.note: The repair costs a few thousand dollars because so much of the engine must be taken apart.

items.t: Turbochargers fail on the 650i
items.job: Replace one turbocharger (rebuilt BMW unit)
items.note: BimmerWorld lists a BMW rebuilt N63 turbo for the 2013-2018 650i at $3,518 including a $590 refundable core. RepairPal puts the total at $3,839-$4,787 for the 650i; labor hours here are the gap between that total and the part price. Replacing both turbos roughly doubles the cost.

items.t: High-pressure fuel pump fails
items.job: Replace high-pressure fuel pump
items.note: The V8 pump costs more than the 6-cylinder's.

items.t: Fuel injectors fail on the 650i V8
items.job: Replace fuel injectors
items.note: Price depends on how many injectors are replaced.

items.t: Valve cover and oil separator leak on the 640i
items.job: Replace valve cover with gasket

items.t: Thermostat and plastic coolant pipes fail on the 640i
items.job: Replace thermostat

items.t: Trunk seals leak and the carpet gets wet
items.job: Replace trunk seal

items.note: Valve stem seal repair, if needed, costs a few thousand dollars.

items.t: Valve cover and crankcase vent valve leak on the 3.0L six
items.job: Replace valve cover with built-in vent valve
